text.title: Project file layout and bootstrap contract
text.summary: The workflow's contract is a fixed on-disk layout under the project's `.product/` folder. Master-prompt + state + decisions + tasks + research are the five durable artifacts. Every subagent reads its inputs from disk; the orchestrator never pastes long prompts.

section.title: Directory layout
section.p: Every project driven by this workflow has a `.product/` folder at its root with this shape.
section.code: .product/ ├── master-prompt.md # WHAT we build, WHY, conventions, /faion resources ├── prfaq.md # Phase 2.5 concept gate; frontmatter carries the verdict ├── constitution.md # standing rules locked after Phase 2; read by Phases 3-6 ├── state.md # CURRENT phase, in-flight tasks, one-line log ├── decisions/decisions.md # append-only architectural decisions ├── tasks/NN-<slug>.md # per-task briefs read by subagents ├── research/NN-<slug>.md # subagent outputs land here BEFORE summary └── (optional) features/NN-<slug>/ # SDD feature folders once Phase 3 lands
section.p: The folder names and the file shape are the contract. Project content (vision, stack, billing model) is project-specific; the file layout is not.

section.title: master-prompt.md
section.p: Single entry point. Every agent (orchestrator and every subagent) reads it first. Holds the project vision, architecture sketch, phase list, conventions inherited from the workspace, and the list of `/faion` resources to invoke per phase. It is rewritten only when the vision itself changes; phase progression does not edit it.

section.title: constitution.md
section.p: Written once by the orchestrator after Phase 2 locks the stack: at most 20 standing rules, each with one sentence of why. Phases 3-6 read it, and planning subagents cite it by rule id (`R-NN`). `decisions/decisions.md` remains append-only history; the constitution is the standing set, so a rule that goes stale is amended in place rather than appended to. If the project has no rules worth stating, the file is not written — an empty constitution is worse than none, because later phases read it as authoritative.

section.title: state.md
section.p: Refreshed every cron tick. Holds: current phase, in-flight subagents, last action, next action, parked open questions. The log section is one line per tick — symbols not paragraphs.
section.reference: Tick semantics and the log format.

rule.statement: Architectural decisions MUST be appended to `decisions/decisions.md` with: ISO date, decision (one sentence), rationale (why this beats alternatives), alternatives considered (list with rejection reasons). Past entries are NEVER rewritten.
rule.rationale: External callers (commits, SDD tickets, code review) cite decisions by date. Rewriting silently breaks citations. Append-only plus a chosen-vs-rejected pair makes the trail trustworthy across compactions and restarts.

rule.statement: `state.md` MUST carry a one-line index per decision (ISO date + one sentence + anchor). The orchestrator and its subagents read the full `decisions/decisions.md` body only when a task brief names the anchor.
rule.rationale: An append-only log grows monotonically, so loading it whole on every tick re-pays its full cost for decisions the current phase cannot act on. The index line is enough to decide whether the body is worth a read. Loading discipline, not the entry template, is what keeps a decision log affordable over a multi-week run.

section.title: tasks/ and research/
section.p: Each task brief under `tasks/NN-<slug>.md` is self-contained: goal, required output structure, `/faion` resources to use, search tool chain, constraints, return-summary word cap. The matching subagent saves its full output to `research/NN-<slug>.md` before returning the bounded summary to the orchestrator.

rule.statement: Subagents MUST save full output to `research/NN-<slug>.md` BEFORE returning a summary. The orchestrator's summary read is bounded; full output is not re-read unless an architectural decision depends on a specific quote.
rule.rationale: If the summary alone could contain the full output, the orchestrator carries N copies of it across ticks. Persisting on disk keeps the orchestrator lean and lets future ticks re-source detail without re-running the subagent.

section.title: Bootstrap step
section.p: On first invocation, the orchestrator creates `.product/` with empty `state.md` (phase 1 pending) and a fresh `master-prompt.md` derived from the operator's one-line ask. The first task briefs (one per Phase 1 research dimension) are written before any subagent dispatch. After bootstrap, the cron loop takes over.

rule.statement: Every directory created by this workflow MUST get a `CLAUDE.md` containing exactly the one line `@AGENTS.md`. This includes `.product/`, `.product/tasks/`, `.product/research/`, and any `features/<id>/` folder.
rule.rationale: The one-line bridge is pure routing: it costs one line, it is not model-written prose, and it makes the directory reachable from either agent runtime. This half of the convention is free and stays mandatory.

rule.statement: The matching `AGENTS.md` is a STUB, not generated prose: at most 30 lines, carrying commands, conventions and boundaries only — never a directory listing, a dependency list, or an architecture overview. The orchestrator MUST NOT auto-generate an `AGENTS.md` body; it writes the stub and the operator confirms or replaces it at the next gate. An unconfirmed stub does NOT block phase advance, and a directory the operator declines to describe keeps a stub of zero content lines.
rule.rationale: The `AGENTS.md` body is not free: it is re-read on every tick of every future session. The only controlled study of the format (Gloaguen et al., ETH Zurich + LogicStar, arXiv, February 2026) measured machine-generated context files as a net loss — −0.5% on SWE-bench Lite, worse in five of eight settings — while human-written ones bought roughly +4% success for +19% inference cost, and every variant tested added 20-23% cost and 14-22% reasoning tokens. Repository-overview sections specifically measured unhelpful, because the agent derives them from the files anyway. A bounded, human-confirmed stub keeps the routing benefit and stops paying for generated prose that measurably hurts.

antipattern.description: Bootstrapping eight nested `AGENTS.md` files as part of creating the project tree, each opened with a generated repository-overview and dependency section.
antipattern.reason: The tax is paid on every tick of every future session, for content the agent reconstructs from the files themselves — and the measured effect of generated context files is negative, not neutral. The cost is certain; the benefit is not.
